name: gauge
title: Gauge
description: A reading on a dial: an arc that fills as far as the value has come.
use: One measurement a reader takes in at a glance, where the figure is the point and the arc says how near the limit it is: a load, a score, a quota. Write the reading in aria-valuenow and again as the text of gauge-value, with its unit.

instead.when: The reading stands in a row or a form beside its label and needs no figure of its own
It is a task that completes, not a measurement
The reader needs the figure and how it moved, without a picture of a range

platform.feature: Typed attr(), as in attr(aria-valuenow type(<number>))
platform.fallback: The gauge does not read aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax: set --gauge-value in a style attribute as well, and --gauge-min and --gauge-max when the range is not 0 to 100

classes.name: gauge
classes.description: The dial, 120px across, on an element with role="meter", an accessible name and the reading in aria-valuenow: two thirds of a ring, open at the foot, filled with ink as far as the reading

classes.name: gauge-value
classes.description: The reading as text, in large tabular figures at the middle of the dial

classes.name: gauge-label
classes.description: One quiet word under the figure, between the two ends of the arc; without it the figure stands at the middle

states.name: value
states.description: The reading, between aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax or 0 and 100. The fill eases to each new reading

properties.name: --gauge-value
properties.description: The reading. It comes from aria-valuenow where typed attr() is supported; set it by hand elsewhere

properties.name: --gauge-min
properties.description: The foot of the range. It comes from aria-valuemin where typed attr() is supported

properties.name: --gauge-max
properties.description: The top of the range. It comes from aria-valuemax where typed attr() is supported

properties.name: --gauge-color
properties.description: The ink of the fill; the track is the same color stepped back. Set a status color when the reading is one, and say so in words

example: 72% Memory
